---
title: "Preservation investigation protocol"
---

This book is the operating record for approved FreeMPE preservation research. It
does not authorize or run device experiments automatically. Each numbered page
proposes one bounded experiment, states what to preserve, and gives an explicit
evaluation rule.

Work through the pages in order with one device at a time. The first run uses
the stable identifier `seaboard-block-01`; replace it only after the device
register records the exact model privately.

Before opening Stage 1, create a human-intent specification with
`$speckit-specify`. Select the **preservation investigation** route and set its
execution status to `ready to run` only after its safety invariants, observation
artifacts, and stop conditions are complete. Keep the specification with its
other Spec Kit artifacts under `../specs/`.

## Evidence boundary

- `../evidence/records/` contains reviewable observations and conclusions.
- `../evidence/private/` is for serial numbers, Bluetooth addresses, and other
  personal identifiers. It is deliberately not version-controlled.
- `../evidence/captures/` is local staging for raw traffic captures. Review a
  capture's contents and redistribution status before moving a selected,
  shareable derivative into the repository.

An observation is not a conclusion. Record the device, firmware, host, method,
and result before updating any compatibility claim.

## Sequence

1. Register the test host and device.
2. Establish an offline connection.
3. Characterize standard MIDI and MPE behaviour.
4. Test an independent sound source.
5. Test persistence across a power cycle.
6. Observe the official configuration tool offline.
7. Capture one configuration change, only after the safe baseline exists.
8. Write a dependency map and choose the next investigation.
